courses.title: General Physics (PHY 101/102)
courses.description: Mechanics, energy, heat, electricity and waves — the 100 Level physics that underpins physiology, radiography and biomedical engineering.

topics.title: Units, Dimensions and Vectors
topics.summary: SI units, dimensional analysis, scalars and vectors.

material.heading: SI units and dimensions
material.body: The seven SI base quantities are length (metre), mass (kilogram), time (second), electric current (ampere), temperature (kelvin), amount of substance (mole) and luminous intensity (candela). Derived units combine base units: newton = kg·m·s⁻², joule = N·m = kg·m²·s⁻², watt = J/s, pascal = N/m². Dimensional analysis uses [M], [L], [T] to check equations: velocity [LT⁻¹], acceleration [LT⁻²], force [MLT⁻²], energy [ML²T⁻²].
keyPoints: 7 SI base units: m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd
An equation must be dimensionally consistent

material.heading: Scalars and vectors
material.body: Scalars have magnitude only (mass, speed, temperature, energy, time). Vectors have magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, momentum). Vectors are added by the triangle or parallelogram law; perpendicular vectors combine by Pythagoras: R = √(A² + B²). A vector F at angle θ to the horizontal has components F cos θ (horizontal) and F sin θ (vertical).
keyPoints: Speed is scalar; velocity is vector
Components: F cos θ and F sin θ

topics.title: Motion and Newton's Laws
topics.summary: Equations of motion, free fall, Newton's three laws, momentum and friction.

material.heading: Kinematics
material.body: For uniform acceleration: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as; s = ½(u + v)t. Near Earth's surface objects in free fall accelerate at g ≈ 9.8 m/s² (often taken as 10 m/s²). On a velocity–time graph, the gradient is acceleration and the area under the graph is displacement.
keyPoints: v = u + at; s = ut + ½at²; v² = u² + 2as
v–t graph: slope = acceleration, area = displacement

material.heading: Dynamics
material.body: Newton's first law (inertia): a body stays at rest or moves uniformly unless acted on by a net external force. Second law: F = ma (force equals rate of change of momentum). Third law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Momentum p = mv is conserved in the absence of external forces; impulse = FΔt = change in momentum. Friction opposes motion; limiting friction F = μR, where μ is the coefficient of friction and R the normal reaction. Weight W = mg.

topics.title: Work, Energy, Power and Heat
topics.summary: Work–energy theorem, kinetic and potential energy, power, efficiency and heat transfer.

material.heading: Work, energy and power
material.body: Work W = Fs cos θ (joules). Kinetic energy KE = ½mv²; gravitational potential energy PE = mgh. Energy is conserved: it changes form but is not created or destroyed. Power is the rate of doing work, P = W/t (watts); also P = Fv. Efficiency = (useful output ÷ input) × 100%.

material.heading: Heat
material.body: Heat energy Q = mcΔθ, where c is specific heat capacity (water: 4,200 J/kg/K, which is why water buffers body temperature). Latent heat Q = mL is absorbed or released during a change of state without a change in temperature; evaporation of sweat cools the body using latent heat of vaporisation. Heat transfers by conduction (solids), convection (fluids) and radiation (electromagnetic waves, no medium needed). Temperature scales: K = °C + 273.
keyPoints: Sweating cools via latent heat of vaporisation

topics.title: Electricity and Magnetism
topics.summary: Charge, current, Ohm's law, resistors in circuits, electrical power and electromagnetism.

material.heading: Current electricity
material.body: Current I is the rate of flow of charge, I = Q/t (amperes). Ohm's law: V = IR for ohmic conductors at constant temperature. Resistors in series add: R = R1 + R2 + …; in parallel: 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + …, giving a total smaller than the smallest resistor. Electrical power P = IV = I²R = V²/R; energy used = Pt (the kilowatt-hour is the commercial unit). Resistance R = ρL/A depends on resistivity, length and cross-sectional area.

material.heading: Magnetism and electromagnetism
material.body: A current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field (Oersted). A conductor in a magnetic field experiences a force F = BIL sin θ, the principle of the electric motor (Fleming's left-hand rule). A changing magnetic flux induces an emf (Faraday's law), with direction opposing the change (Lenz's law) — the basis of generators and transformers (Vs/Vp = Ns/Np). MRI scanners use strong superconducting magnets measured in tesla.
keyPoints: Faraday: changing flux induces emf; Lenz: opposes the change

topics.title: Waves, Sound and Light
topics.summary: Wave properties, sound and ultrasound, reflection, refraction, lenses and the electromagnetic spectrum.

material.heading: Waves and sound
material.body: Waves transfer energy without transferring matter. Transverse waves (light, all electromagnetic waves) vibrate perpendicular to the direction of travel; longitudinal waves (sound) vibrate parallel to it. Wave speed v = fλ. Sound needs a medium and travels faster in solids than in air (~340 m/s in air, ~1,540 m/s in soft tissue). Humans hear 20 Hz–20 kHz; ultrasound (> 20 kHz, clinically 2–15 MHz) is used in medical imaging because it reflects at tissue interfaces.
keyPoints: Sound is longitudinal and needs a medium
Ultrasound > 20 kHz; ~1,540 m/s in soft tissue

material.heading: Light and the EM spectrum
material.body: Reflection: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection. Refraction is bending of light as it changes speed between media; refractive index n = sin i / sin r = c/v. Total internal reflection occurs beyond the critical angle and is used in optical fibres and endoscopes. Converging (convex) lenses correct hypermetropia; diverging (concave) lenses correct myopia. Lens power in dioptres = 1/f (in metres). The EM spectrum in order of increasing frequency: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays; all travel at 3 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum.
keyPoints: Myopia: concave lens; hypermetropia: convex lens
